title: O-NET ม.6 ชุดฝึกที่ 2

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: Visiting Ton in hospital

dialogue.speaker: Ton
dialogue.text: Much better, thanks. The doctor says I can go home on Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Waan
dialogue.text: That's great news. I brought you some oranges and the notes from our chemistry class.

dialogue.speaker: Ton
dialogue.text: Oh, you didn't have to. ___2___

dialogue.speaker: Waan
dialogue.text: It's nothing. You'd do the same for me.

dialogue.speaker: Ton
dialogue.text: By the way, how long can you stay? Visiting hours end at seven.

dialogue.speaker: Waan
dialogue.text: ___3___ I'll come again on Wednesday, though.

dialogue.speaker: Ton
dialogue.text: OK. See you then, and say hi to everyone at school.

options: How often do you come here?
What did you have for lunch?
items.explanationTh: Ton ตอบว่า "Much better, thanks." (ดีขึ้นมากแล้ว) จึงต้องเป็นคำถามถามอาการ How are you feeling today? ตัวเลือกอื่นถามเรื่องอาหาร ความถี่ หมอ หรือเวลา ซึ่งไม่เข้ากับคำตอบ
Ton กำลังขอบคุณที่ Waan นำของมาเยี่ยม และ Waan ตอบรับคำขอบคุณว่า "It's nothing." จึงต้องเป็นคำขอบคุณ How kind of you! ส่วน Don't mention it. เป็นคำตอบรับคำขอบคุณ ไม่ใช่คำขอบคุณเอง

คำถาม how long can you stay? ถามว่าจะอยู่ได้นานเท่าไร และประโยคต่อมา "I'll come again on Wednesday, though." แสดงว่าอยู่ได้ไม่นาน จึงตอบ Not long, I'm afraid. ส่วน Since... และ For two weeks last year เป็นเรื่องอดีต

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: At a clothes shop

dialogue.speaker: Assistant
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Nat
dialogue.text: Yes, please. I bought this shirt here yesterday, but it's too small for me.

dialogue.speaker: Assistant
dialogue.text: I see. Have you got the receipt?

dialogue.speaker: Assistant
dialogue.text: Thank you. Would you like a bigger size or your money back?

dialogue.speaker: Nat
dialogue.text: ___3___ Do you have it in large?

dialogue.speaker: Assistant
dialogue.text: Let me check. Yes, here you are. You can try it on over there.

items.explanationTh: พนักงานร้านเสนอความช่วยเหลือลูกค้า และ Nat ตอบว่า "Yes, please." จึงต้องเป็น Can I help you? ส่วน Can you help me? เป็นคำพูดของลูกค้า และ Are you ready to order? ใช้ในร้านอาหาร
พนักงานถามว่ามีใบเสร็จไหม แล้วตอบว่า "Thank you." แสดงว่า Nat ยื่นใบเสร็จให้ จึงตอบ Yes, here it is. ตัวเลือกอื่นไม่ได้ตอบคำถามเรื่องใบเสร็จ

options: I'd like my money back, please.
items.explanationTh: Nat ถามต่อว่า "Do you have it in large?" แสดงว่าต้องการเปลี่ยนเป็นไซซ์ใหญ่ขึ้น จึงตอบ I'd rather change it ส่วนการขอเงินคืนขัดกับประโยคถัดไป

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: A phone call to a music school

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Good morning, Melody House Music School. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Fern
dialogue.text: Hello, this is Fern Suwannarat. I have a piano lesson at four this afternoon, but I need to move it.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: No problem. ___2___

dialogue.speaker: Fern
dialogue.text: Is Thursday at the same time possible?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Let me see... Sorry, Thursday is full. How about Friday at five?

dialogue.speaker: Fern
dialogue.text: ___3___ Thank you so much.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: You're welcome. See you on Friday, Fern.

options: Can I speak to Fern, please?
items.explanationTh: พนักงานรับโทรศัพท์ทักทายแล้วถามว่าจะให้ช่วยอะไร Fern จึงบอกธุระของตน ส่วน May I take your order? ใช้ในร้านอาหาร และ Can I speak to Fern? ไม่สมเหตุผลเพราะ Fern เป็นผู้โทรมาเอง

options: Why didn't you come last week?
How long have you played the piano?
How much does a lesson cost?
When would you like to come instead?
items.explanationTh: Fern ตอบว่า "Is Thursday at the same time possible?" ซึ่งเป็นการเสนอวันเวลาใหม่ คำถามจึงต้องถามว่าอยากมาวันไหนแทน
Fern ขอบคุณ และพนักงานตอบว่า "See you on Friday" แสดงว่า Fern ตกลงวันศุกร์ห้าโมงเย็น จึงตอบ Friday at five is fine. ตัวเลือกอื่นเป็นการปฏิเสธหรือแสดงความเสียใจ

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: A favour from a neighbour

dialogue.speaker: Joe
dialogue.text: Excuse me, Mrs. Lim. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Lim
dialogue.text: Of course, Joe. What is it?

dialogue.speaker: Joe
dialogue.text: My family is going to Hua Hin this weekend. Could you feed our cat, Mochi, while we're away?

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Lim
dialogue.text: ___2___ I love cats. How often does she eat?

dialogue.speaker: Joe
dialogue.text: Twice a day, morning and evening. I'll leave her food and our spare key with you.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Lim
dialogue.text: All right. ___3___

dialogue.speaker: Joe
dialogue.text: Thanks so much, Mrs. Lim. I owe you one.

options: Could I ask you a favour?
items.explanationTh: Mrs. Lim ตอบว่า "Of course. What is it?" และ Joe ขอให้ช่วยให้อาหารแมว จึงต้องเป็นการขอความช่วยเหลือ Could I ask you a favour?
Mrs. Lim บอกต่อว่า "I love cats." และถามว่าแมวกินบ่อยแค่ไหน แสดงว่ายินดีช่วย จึงตอบ I'd be happy to. ตัวเลือกปฏิเสธขัดกับบริบท

options: Don't worry. Just enjoy your trip.
items.explanationTh: Mrs. Lim ตกลงรับดูแลแมวแล้ว (All right.) จึงควรบอกให้ Joe สบายใจและเที่ยวให้สนุก ส่วนเรื่องแพ้แมวหรือให้พาแมวไปด้วยขัดกับที่เธอเพิ่งตกลง

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: Planning a group poster

dialogue.speaker: Oat
dialogue.text: OK, our poster on recycling is due next Tuesday. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Kaew
dialogue.text: I can find the pictures and print them.

dialogue.speaker: Oat
dialogue.text: Great. And Pete, can you write the text?

dialogue.speaker: Pete
dialogue.text: ___2___ I have a football match on Saturday, so I'll do it on Sunday.

dialogue.speaker: Oat
dialogue.text: That's fine. I'll put everything together on Monday.

dialogue.speaker: Kaew
dialogue.text: Sorry, Oat, your voice is breaking up on my phone. ___3___

dialogue.speaker: Oat
dialogue.text: I said I'll put everything together on Monday.

options: Who wants to do which part?
Where did you buy the poster?
items.explanationTh: Kaew ตอบว่า "I can find the pictures..." ซึ่งเป็นการอาสารับงานส่วนหนึ่ง คำถามจึงต้องเป็นการแบ่งงาน Who wants to do which part?
Pete รับปากและบอกว่าจะเขียนวันอาทิตย์ จึงตอบรับว่า Sure, no problem. ส่วน I've already done it. ขัดกับ "I'll do it on Sunday"
Kaew ได้ยินไม่ชัดเพราะเสียงขาด ๆ หาย ๆ และ Oat พูดซ้ำว่า "I said..." จึงต้องเป็นการขอให้พูดซ้ำ Could you repeat that, please?

groups.instructionTh: อ่านป้ายประกาศ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Museum sign
groups.text:
WELCOME TO THE BAN NAM SAI FOLK MUSEUM
Opening hours: Tuesday–Sunday, 9:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. (last entry 4:00 p.m.). Closed on Mondays.
Tickets: Adults 60 baht · Students (with ID card) 30 baht · Children under 7 free
Please note:
• Bags larger than a school backpack must be left in the lockers next to the ticket office. Lockers are free.
• Photos are welcome, but please do not use a flash in the Textile Room. Bright light can damage the old cloth.
• Do not touch the objects unless you see a green hand sign.
• Food and drinks are only allowed in the garden café.
Free guided tours in Thai and English start at 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. from the main hall.

items.stem: Which of the following can visitors do for free?
options: Eat lunch in the main hall
Take flash photos of the cloth
items.explanationTh: ป้ายระบุ "Free guided tours in Thai and English" ทัวร์นำชมจึงฟรี ส่วนตั๋วผู้ใหญ่ราคา 60 บาท ห้ามใช้แฟลชในห้องผ้า วันจันทร์ปิด และกินอาหารได้เฉพาะในคาเฟ่

items.stem: How much do two students with ID cards and their five-year-old brother pay in total?
items.explanationTh: นักเรียนที่มีบัตรคนละ 30 บาท 2 คน = 60 บาท และเด็กอายุต่ำกว่า 7 ปีเข้าฟรี (Children under 7 free) รวมเป็น 60 บาท

items.stem: Why is flash photography not allowed in the Textile Room?
options: It can harm the old fabric.
items.explanationTh: ป้ายเขียนว่า "Bright light can damage the old cloth." แสงแฟลชทำให้ผ้าเก่าเสียหาย ส่วน Photos are not allowed anywhere ผิดเพราะป้ายบอกว่า Photos are welcome

items.stem: Which visitor is following the museum rules?
options: Lek, who arrives at 4:15 p.m. to buy a ticket
Ann, who touches a vase with no sign near it
Dao, who eats her sandwich in the garden café
Max, who takes a large suitcase into the exhibition
Bo, who comes to see the museum on a Monday
items.explanationTh: อาหารและเครื่องดื่มอนุญาตเฉพาะใน garden café ดังนั้น Dao ทำถูกกฎ ส่วนคนอื่นผิด เช่น เข้าหลัง 4:00 น. จับวัตถุที่ไม่มีป้ายมือสีเขียว นำกระเป๋าใหญ่เข้าไป หรือมาวันจันทร์ที่ปิด

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: A note on the kitchen table
groups.text:
Hi Somchai,
Welcome home! Sorry I'm not here — I had to take Grandma to the dentist, and we won't be back until about 7. Dinner is in the fridge: just heat the chicken soup for three minutes in the microwave. Please don't use the big pot on the stove; the handle is loose and I don't want you to get hurt. If you go out, take the spare key from the blue box by the door and lock up. Oh, and could you bring the washing in from the garden if it starts to rain?
See you later,
Helen

items.stem: Why is Helen not at home?
options: She has her own dental appointment.
She is at the doctor's with Somchai.
She is helping a family member.
She is working late at the office.
items.explanationTh: Helen เขียนว่า "I had to take Grandma to the dentist" คือพาคุณยายไปหาหมอฟัน ไม่ใช่ไปหาหมอฟันเองหรือไปทำงาน

items.stem: What does Helen want Somchai to do with the soup?
options: Cook it in the big pot
Take it out to the garden
Warm it up in the microwave
Eat it cold from the fridge
items.explanationTh: ข้อความบอกว่า "just heat the chicken soup for three minutes in the microwave" และห้ามใช้หม้อใหญ่เพราะหูจับหลวม

items.stem: The word "loose" in the note is closest in meaning to ____.
items.explanationTh: "the handle is loose and I don't want you to get hurt" หูจับหม้อหลวม คือยึดไม่แน่น จึงอาจทำให้บาดเจ็บได้

items.stem: Which of the following is TRUE according to the note?
options: The spare key is kept in the garden.
Somchai should lock the door if he goes out.
Helen and Grandma will be back at about 5.
Somchai must stay at home until Helen returns.
Somchai has to cook dinner for everyone.
items.explanationTh: Helen เขียนว่า "If you go out, take the spare key... and lock up." ส่วนกุญแจอยู่ในกล่องสีฟ้าข้างประตู และจะกลับประมาณ 1 ทุ่ม (about 7)

groups.instructionTh: อ่านเรื่อง แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Greetings from the farm!
groups.text:
Hi Nam,

I'm writing from my uncle's farm near Ashford Creek, where I'm spending the school holidays. There's no Wi-Fi in the house, so I'm sending this from the library in town, which we visit every Saturday.

Life here is very different from the city. I get up at half past five every morning to help my uncle milk the cows. At first I hated it, but now I actually enjoy the quiet before sunrise. After breakfast, my cousin Libby and I feed the chickens and collect the eggs. Yesterday I found fourteen eggs — a new record!

The hardest job is fixing fences. The farm is so big that it takes us a whole day to check them all. My hands were sore for days afterwards, but my uncle says I'm getting stronger.

In the evenings we play board games because there is no TV signal. I've become really good at a game called Farmyard Rush, and I've beaten Libby five times in a row. She says it's just luck!

I'll be back home on the 20th. Could you keep copies of the chemistry notes from the classes I'm missing? I'll buy you a mango smoothie as a thank-you.

Write back soon,
Jamie

items.stem: Which job on the farm does Jamie find the hardest?
items.explanationTh: Jamie เขียนว่า "The hardest job is fixing fences." เพราะฟาร์มใหญ่ ต้องตรวจรั้วทั้งวัน

items.stem: Why does Jamie send the email from the library?
options: The farmhouse has no Internet connection.
He works at the library on Saturdays.
The library is quieter than the farm.
Libby uses the house computer all day.
items.explanationTh: Jamie เขียนว่า "There's no Wi-Fi in the house, so I'm sending this from the library" จึงเป็นเพราะที่บ้านไม่มีอินเทอร์เน็ต

items.stem: How have Jamie's feelings about getting up early changed?
options: He liked it at first but now hates it.
He still finds it very hard.
He never gets up early on the farm.
He disliked it at first but now enjoys it.
items.explanationTh: "At first I hated it, but now I actually enjoy the quiet before sunrise." แสดงว่าตอนแรกไม่ชอบ แต่ตอนนี้ชอบแล้ว

items.stem: The word "sore" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ____.
items.explanationTh: หลังซ่อมรั้วทั้งวัน มือของ Jamie "sore for days" หมายถึงเจ็บปวด คำว่า strong เป็นตัวลวงเพราะลุงบอกว่าเขาแข็งแรงขึ้น แต่ไม่ได้หมายถึงมือ sore

items.stem: What will Jamie do for Nam when he gets home?
options: Take Nam to his uncle's farm
Teach Nam a new board game
items.explanationTh: Jamie เขียนว่า "I'll buy you a mango smoothie as a thank-you." เพื่อขอบคุณที่ Nam เก็บโน้ตให้ ส่วนโน้ตเคมีเป็นของที่ Nam จะเก็บให้ Jamie ไม่ใช่กลับกัน

groups.instructionTh: อ่านเรื่อง แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Green Corner: my tiny plant business
groups.text:
When our school announced a Business Week fair last term, most of my classmates decided to sell snacks. I wanted to try something different, so I sold plants.

My idea was simple. My grandmother has dozens of pothos and spider plants on her balcony, and they grow very quickly. With her permission, I cut small pieces from them and put them in glasses of water. After two weeks, each piece had grown roots. I planted them in old yoghurt cups that I collected from neighbours and decorated with paint.

I sold each small plant for 25 baht. On the first day, I sold only six because people walked straight past me to the food stalls. Then my friend Pim suggested a sign that said "Easy plants for busy students — water once a week!" After that, sales grew quickly, and by the end of the week I had sold 58 plants.

My costs were very low: I spent about 200 baht on soil and paint. I gave part of the money to my grandmother, who refused at first, and I used the rest to buy a better pair of garden scissors.

The most important lesson? A good product is not enough. You also need to tell people why they need it.

items.stem: What is the blog mainly about?
options: Why students should not sell snacks
How to look after spider plants at home
The history of the school's Business Week
Why the writer's grandmother loves gardening
How the writer ran a successful plant stall
items.explanationTh: บล็อกเล่าตั้งแต่ไอเดีย การเตรียมต้นไม้ การขาย จนถึงบทเรียนที่ได้ จึงเป็นเรื่องการขายต้นไม้ในงานโรงเรียนจนประสบความสำเร็จ

items.stem: Where did the plant cuttings come from?
options: A garden shop near the school
items.explanationTh: "My grandmother has dozens of pothos and spider plants on her balcony... I cut small pieces from them" ส่วนเพื่อนบ้านให้แค่ถ้วยโยเกิร์ตเก่า ไม่ใช่ต้นไม้

items.stem: Why did sales increase after the first day?
options: The plants were moved into bigger cups.
A sign told students why the plants suited them.
The writer's grandmother helped sell them.
items.explanationTh: หลังจาก Pim แนะนำป้าย "Easy plants for busy students — water once a week!" ยอดขายก็เพิ่มขึ้น ป้ายบอกว่าต้นไม้เหมาะกับนักเรียนที่ยุ่ง ส่วนราคายังคง 25 บาทเท่าเดิม

items.stem: How much money did the writer get from plant sales during the week, before paying for costs?
items.explanationTh: ขายได้ 58 ต้น ต้นละ 25 บาท = 58 × 25 = 1,450 บาท (ยังไม่หักต้นทุน) ส่วน 150 บาทคือยอดขายวันแรก (6 ต้น) และ 200 บาทคือค่าใช้จ่าย

items.stem: What lesson does the writer want readers to learn?
options: Plants are hard to grow from cuttings.
Family members should not be paid.
Food is the best thing to sell.
Explaining a product's value is important.
items.explanationTh: ประโยคสุดท้าย "A good product is not enough. You also need to tell people why they need it." คือต้องบอกให้คนรู้ว่าสินค้ามีประโยชน์อย่างไร

groups.instructionTh: อ่านเรื่อง แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Pond's Menu
groups.text:
Every evening after school, Pond helped his aunt at her noodle stall in the Saphan Khao night market. Aunt Wan cooked, and Pond took orders and washed bowls.

One evening, Aunt Wan asked him to make a menu in English. "More tourists come here now," she said. "You study English at school, so you can do it." Pond felt proud, but also nervous. That night he wrote the menu carefully with a dictionary beside him, and the next day he hung it above the stall.

For a week, very few tourists ordered anything. Most of them read the menu, smiled strangely and walked away. Pond could not understand why.

Then a young backpacker stopped and laughed, but kindly. "Excuse me," she said, pointing at the sign. "I think you mean 'fried noodles', not 'fired noodles'. Fired noodles sound like they've lost their job!" Pond's face turned red, but he laughed too. The backpacker, whose name was Clara, helped him check the rest of the menu while she ate a bowl of noodles with pork.

The next evening, Pond hung up the new menu. By nine o'clock, Aunt Wan had sold out. Since then, Pond has always asked a customer to read every new sign before he puts it up.

items.stem: Why did Aunt Wan ask Pond to write the English menu?
options: He wanted to earn some extra money.
He was the best cook in the family.
He was learning English at school.
The old menu had been lost.
A tourist had asked her to do it.
items.explanationTh: Aunt Wan บอกว่า "You study English at school, so you can do it." จึงให้ Pond ทำเมนูเพราะเขาเรียนภาษาอังกฤษ

items.stem: Why did most tourists probably walk away during the first week?
options: Aunt Wan could not speak English.
The menu had an English mistake.
items.explanationTh: นักท่องเที่ยวอ่านเมนูแล้วยิ้มแปลก ๆ และเดินจากไป ต่อมา Clara ชี้ว่าเขียน 'fired noodles' ผิดแทน 'fried noodles' จึงอนุมานได้ว่าเพราะเมนูสะกดผิด

items.stem: The phrase "sold out" in the last paragraph means that Aunt Wan ____.
options: had lost a lot of money
had no food left to sell
had sold the stall to someone
items.explanationTh: sold out หมายถึงขายหมด หลังเปลี่ยนเมนูใหม่ที่ถูกต้อง ร้านขายดีจนหมดภายในสามทุ่ม

items.stem: In paragraph 4, who does "she" in "while she ate a bowl of noodles" refer to?

groups.instructionTh: อ่านเรื่อง แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: The Library of Things
groups.text:
In the town of Riverton, people can now borrow a drill as easily as a novel. Last year, the town library opened a "Library of Things" in a small room next to the children's section. Instead of books, its shelves hold more than 300 useful items, from ladders and sewing machines to camping tents and karaoke sets.

The idea came from a librarian named Marisa Kent. "Many people buy a tool, use it once, and then keep it in a cupboard for years," she explains. "Sharing is cheaper for families, and it means fewer things end up in rubbish bins."

Borrowing works just like it does for books. Members show their library card, and they can take up to three items for one week. There is no fee, but borrowers must clean items before returning them. If something is broken, the library asks for a small amount of money to repair it.

The most popular item so far is a pressure washer, which has been borrowed 87 times. Board games and a bread-making machine are also in high demand. Volunteers check every item when it comes back and teach short workshops on Saturdays, such as how to use a sewing machine safely.

Not everything has gone smoothly. In the first month, two tents came back wet and smelly. Now the library gives borrowers a simple checklist with each item.

items.stem: Where in the town library is the Library of Things?

In a garden behind the library
In a room beside the children's section
On the shelves with the novels
In the main hall by the entrance
items.explanationTh: บทความระบุว่าเปิด "Library of Things" "in a small room next to the children's section"

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทความเกี่ยวกับวัฒนธรรม แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Afternoon Tea: More Than a Cup of Tea
groups.text:
In Britain, "afternoon tea" is not just a drink. It is a light meal, usually served between three and five o'clock. The custom is often said to have started in the 1840s, when a nineteenth-century English duchess felt hungry during the long gap between lunch and a late dinner. She began asking for tea, bread and butter, and cake in her room, and soon she was inviting friends to join her. Before long, it became a fashionable social event.

A traditional afternoon tea is served on a stand with three plates. Small sandwiches, such as cucumber or egg, are on the bottom plate. Scones are in the middle, and cakes and sweets are on top. Guests usually eat from the bottom to the top, so they finish with something sweet.

There are a few polite habits to remember. Stir your tea gently, without hitting the sides of the cup, and leave the spoon on the saucer, not in the cup. Contrary to a popular belief, raising your little finger when you hold the cup is not considered good manners. Break scones in half with your hands rather than cutting them with a knife.

Even today, people still argue about scones. In Devon, many people spread cream first and put jam on top; in Cornwall, it is usually jam first. Both sides insist that their way is correct, and the friendly debate often makes people laugh.

Nowadays, most British families do not have afternoon tea every day. Instead, it is a special treat for birthdays and celebrations, or for a day out with friends at a hotel or tea room.

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The history and customs of British afternoon tea
How tea is grown and picked in Britain

A simple recipe for scones and jam
items.explanationTh: บทความเล่าที่มาของ afternoon tea การจัดอาหาร มารยาท และการถกเถียงเรื่องสโคน จึงเป็นเรื่องประวัติและธรรมเนียมของ afternoon tea

options: Her friends were bored after lunch.

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Where Does Rain Come From?
groups.text:
The water you drink today may once have fallen as rain on a mountain, flowed down a river, or even been part of an ocean far away. This is because Earth's water is always moving in a never-ending journey called the water cycle.

The cycle is powered by the sun. When sunlight heats oceans, lakes and rivers, some water turns into an invisible gas called water vapour. This process is called evaporation. Plants also release water vapour through tiny holes in their leaves, which is known as transpiration.

As the warm, moist air rises, it cools. Cool air cannot hold as much water vapour as warm air, so the vapour changes back into tiny drops of liquid water. This is condensation. Millions of these drops gather together to form clouds. You can see the same process on a hot day, when drops appear on the outside of a glass of iced water.

When the drops in a cloud join together and become too heavy, they fall to the ground as precipitation. Depending on the temperature, this may be rain, snow or hail.

Finally, the water collects. Some runs over the land into rivers and back to the sea. Some soaks into the ground and becomes groundwater, which can stay underground for hundreds of years. Then the sun heats the water again, and the cycle continues.

Because of this cycle, the total amount of water on Earth stays almost the same. However, it is not always in the right place at the right time, which is why floods and droughts happen.

items.stem: According to the passage, what can happen to water that soaks into the ground?
options: It changes into water vapour at once.
It can stay underground for a very long time.

items.explanationTh: "Some soaks into the ground and becomes groundwater, which can stay underground for hundreds of years." น้ำใต้ดินอยู่ใต้ดินได้นานหลายร้อยปี

items.stem: According to the passage, what gives the water cycle its energy?

items.explanationTh: บทความยกตัวอย่างนี้ในย่อหน้าเรื่อง condensation ("You can see the same process...") ไอน้ำในอากาศเย็นตัวลงกลายเป็นหยดน้ำ

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Locking Your Digital Door
groups.text:
Most of us would never leave our front door unlocked, yet many people protect their online accounts with passwords that are easy to guess. A recent survey by the computer club at Northgate College found that one in four of its students used their own birthday as a password, and almost half used the same password for every account.

Why is this dangerous? Criminals use computer programs that can try thousands of common passwords in a few seconds. Words like "password", "123456" or a pet's name are usually guessed first. And if you use one password everywhere, a thief who discovers it can open all of your accounts at once — your email, your games and even your bank app.

Experts suggest a simple method: the passphrase. Instead of one short word, choose three or four random words and join them together, for example "purple-kettle-river-jump". A passphrase is long, which makes it hard for a computer to guess, but it is easy for a person to remember.

It also helps to turn on two-step verification. With this feature, you need both your password and a code sent to your phone to log in. Even if someone learns your password, they still cannot get in without your phone.

Finally, never share your password with friends, even close ones. A password is like a toothbrush: use it only yourself, and change it from time to time.

items.explanationTh: บทความอธิบายอันตรายของรหัสผ่านที่เดาง่าย และแนะนำ passphrase การยืนยันตัวตนสองขั้นตอน และการไม่แชร์รหัสผ่าน จึงเป็นเรื่องวิธีรักษาความปลอดภัยของบัญชีออนไลน์

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: The Blue Wave Club
groups.text:
Every second Sunday of the month, while most teenagers are still asleep, about forty students from Laem Thong School are already on Hat Sai Ngam beach with gloves and rice sacks. They are members of the Blue Wave Club, which started three years ago with only five people.

The club was the idea of Kanya Rattana, then a Grade 10 student. "I went swimming one morning and a plastic bag wrapped around my leg," she remembers. "I thought, if I don't do something, who will?" She put up posters around school, and her science teacher agreed to be the club's adviser.

The members do more than just pick up rubbish. They sort everything they collect and record it on a data sheet. Last year, they collected over 1,300 kilograms of waste. The most common items were plastic bottle caps, food wrappers and pieces of fishing net. "The data is useful," explains Kanya. "We sent our results to the local council, and they agreed to put more recycling bins near the food stalls."

Not all the waste comes from beach visitors. Some is carried by the sea from places hundreds of kilometres away. This shows that ocean pollution is a global problem, not just a local one.

The club has also changed its members. "Before, I never thought about how much plastic I used," says Ohm, a Grade 11 member. "Now I bring my own bottle and bag everywhere."

Kanya will graduate next March, but she is not worried. The club now has a team of leaders from every grade, and three nearby schools have started similar clubs.

items.explanationTh: ชมรมเริ่ม "three years ago with only five people" และตอนนี้มีนักเรียนประมาณ 40 คน ส่วนการพบกันคือวันอาทิตย์ที่สองของเดือนเท่านั้น

items.explanationTh: ครูวิทยาศาสตร์ตกลงเป็น adviser ของชมรม คือที่ปรึกษาผู้ให้คำแนะนำและช่วยเหลือ
